subject: Subprocessor delegation variance — DPA escalation & MSA/Order Form redline path
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@cloudcore.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cloudcore.com, procurement@cloudcore.com
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: downstream subprocessor change + DPA redlines

Rohan —

Quick heads up from procurement/legal: one of our integration partners (EdgeStream LLC) has introduced a new analytics subprocessor in their pipeline that will process a subset of telemetry tied to end-user prompts. CloudCore needs Redwood to accept flow-down for this new subprocessor or confirm an alternate mitigation.

Attached are CloudCore's proposed DPA redlines (CloudCore_DPA_redlines_v2.docx) and an excerpt of the MSA Order Form clause they want amended. Key asks:
- Acceptance of EdgeStream as a subprocessor (will require Redwood subproc consent)
- Confirmation of data location and encryption-at-rest details for the delegated processing
- A short-term exception process while EdgeStream completes SOC2 Type II (estimated 45 days)

Can you confirm internal lane for legal review + whether we can accept an exception path (procurement asked for a signed letter rather than full contract amendment). Want to avoid blocking their PO which is on a tight timeline (Q2 close).

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Integrations, CloudCore Systems
Procurement request ID: CC-PO-3319

Attachments: CloudCore_DPA_redlines_v2.docx
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Notice: downstream subprocessor change + DPA redlines

Looping you all in — forwarding CloudCore's notice. Summary: EdgeStream wants to be added as a downstream subprocessor for telemetry enrichment. CloudCore proposes DPA redlines and an Order Form amendment; procurement is pushing for a lightweight exception letter so they can close PO this quarter.

Questions for legal/procurement:
- Does EdgeStream's role trigger our standard subprocessor consent flow or can we use a limited exception (scoped, timeboxed) that includes mandatory SOC2 attestation within 45 days?
- If we accept exception, what approvals are required (legal + security + GC sign-off?)
- Any required redlines on the MSA/Order Form items to preserve Redwood's liability caps & audit rights?

Attachments referenced by CloudCore attached to this mail for your review (see copies in thread).

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: downstream subprocessor change + DPA redlines

Thanks for flagging. Initial read: CloudCore's redlines widen our obligation on audit access and effectively transfer a portion of their indemnity language downstream. Two immediate concerns:

1) Audit scope and timing — CloudCore's draft wants audit rights that include EdgeStream's internal logs; we need to limit to proof-of-controls (SOC2 report + targeted evidence) rather than open-ended forensic access.

2) Liability and flow-down reciprocity — we should not accept a clause that expands our indemnity exposure for a subcontractor we do not control. If CloudCore insists, require a carve-in that restricts liability to breaches caused by Redwood's direct processing or a capped indemnity tied to EdgeStream's negligence.

I suggest:
- Counter-propose acceptance of EdgeStream pending receipt of SOC2 Type II or equivalent attestation within 45 days.
- Provide a timeboxed limited consent letter (templated) that requires immediate encryption confirmations, logging retention, and a documented incident escalation path to Redwood and CloudCore.
- If SOC2 not provided in 45 days, automatic suspension of the EdgeStream delegation (with 30-day remediation).

Karthik — can you validate the technical controls (encryption at rest, key management, region of processing) and supply the control checklist we need to include in the consent letter?

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Jun 2028 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: downstream subprocessor change + DPA redlines

Grace — initial technical assessment below after quick sync with infra-ops:

- EdgeStream claims AES-256 at rest and TLS1.3 in transit; we need KMS details (who holds keys) and whether keys are tenant-scoped or shared.
- Processing region: they listed us-east-1 and eu-west-1; must confirm CloudCore's traffic for our account is only routed to us-east-1 per our Order Form geography. If EdgeStream can process in eu-west-1, we must document that and update DPA accordingly.
- Logging retention: suggest 90 days minimal for telemetry artifacts tied to incidents.

I'll attach a short control checklist for the consent letter and can confirm by EOD when I have the KMS answers.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Security Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_subproc_control_checklist_v1.pdf (stub)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Jun 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: downstream subprocessor change + DPA redlines

Team — I reviewed CloudCore's proposed MSA snippet (they want to amend Order Form Section 4 with explicit flow-down language). My take: procurement's lightweight letter could be acceptable if we:

- Attach Redwood's templated consent letter that includes the control checklist and strict termination clause tied to SOC2 delivery
- Add a short amendment to the Order Form that references the consent letter as the exclusive mechanism for subprocessor delegations for this Account (prevents later unilateral expansions)
- Require a backup plan: if CloudCore can't produce required attestations, Redwood keeps the right to block EdgeStream processing for Redwood-origin data.

If legal + security sign off, procurement can convert the consent letter into a one-page addendum we countersign. Lauren (Legal) — can you draft the consent letter + the minimal Order Form amendment? We should not alter core MSA liability caps.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@cloudcore.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, legal@cloudcore.com
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: downstream subprocessor change + DPA redlines

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Redwood team. CloudCore is OK with the proposed timeboxed consent letter as long as it is signed by both parties and includes the SOC2 delivery milestone. They asked we keep the change non-blocking for 14 days while EdgeStream completes a remediation plan (CloudCore will provide an interim attestation).

Attached: CloudCore has shared an interim attestation and a short EdgeStream technical summary. Can we get a countersigned consent letter by EOD Wed (06/11)? Procurement is prioritizing this for the PO close.

Sanjay

Head of Integrations, CloudCore Systems
